article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Morning Brief
article.dek: The Hurts diagnosis, Monday night's final in Santa Clara, and what to watch as the board flips to Week 7.

items.headline: Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season
paragraphs: Monday brought the biggest news of the week: the Eagles announced that further testing found deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both of Jalen Hurts' lungs. He is clinically stable and expected to recover fully, but he is on blood thinners and cannot take part in contact activities.

That ends his season — and it reshapes Sunday's game in Philadelphia, where the Eagles host the Cowboys. The Week 7 board had not flipped to the new week at press time, so the app's expected starter for Philadelphia has not updated yet. Do not act on a stale board: once the morning refresh lands, run your book's number for Cowboys at Eagles through Check and let the model re-price it.
items.takeaway: Quarterback out for the season = new team. Let the app re-price it before you price anything yourself.

items.headline: Monday night: 49ers hang on, 23-17, and stay perfect
paragraphs: San Francisco is 6-0 after surviving Washington 23-17 in Santa Clara. The 49ers led 23-3 late in the third quarter, then watched the Commanders score 14 straight before a final-play sack ended it. Jayden Daniels threw for 300 yards and two scores in the rally.
The board's Monday cards settle now. Settlement is manual — the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself, so log last night's losers too, not just the winners.
items.takeaway: 49ers 6-0, the NFL's only unbeaten. Log the result honestly and move on to Week 7.

items.headline: Injury report, all in one place
paragraphs: Commanders receiver Terry McLaurin was carted off late in the first quarter with a knee injury. 49ers receiver Mike Evans, who played through a questionable tag, aggravated his Achilles before halftime and did not return.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is off the injury report after throwing for 305 yards in Sunday's win over Atlanta — good timing with the Patriots coming to Chicago Thursday night (8:15 p.m. ET kickoff). Chicago estimated linebacker T.J. Edwards, guard Jonah Jackson, running back Kyle Monangai, and linebacker Jack Sanborn as non-participants Monday.
items.takeaway: Check back in the evening brief: Thursday teams report again, and inactives come about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Weather: nothing to check today
paragraphs: There are no games today, so no weather to worry about. The next outdoor kickoff is Thursday night in Chicago — Patriots at Bears — and kickoff-window weather for that one lands in tomorrow's briefs.
items.takeaway: Weather only matters when there is a game. Next check: Thursday in Chicago.

items.headline: The board has not flipped to Week 7 yet — read this before you bet
paragraphs: As of this morning's build, the app still shows last week's board. The morning refresh is landing the Week 7 slate — 14 games, with the Bills, Jaguars, Chargers, and Commanders on bye. Cards, expected margins, and headline overlays will fill in with the refresh.
Until then, treat any line you see in the app as last week's. The board refreshes every morning and evening — once Week 7 is live, that is your starting point, not your answer.
items.takeaway: A stale board is a trap. Confirm the board says Week 7 before you read a single card.

items.headline: When your book's number is not the board's number, tap Check
paragraphs: The Hurts news broke Monday. Some books may still be repricing Cowboys at Eagles, and your book's price may not match the app's market board at all. That is exactly what Check is for: type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on YOUR price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
-120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. For your actual stake, use the app's staking guidance — it sizes from your bankroll and how aggressive you set it, and it stays deliberately conservative.
items.takeaway: Good news plus a good number beats waiting. If Check says bet at your price, bet it.

items.headline: Learn the Game: closing line value
paragraphs: Closing line value — CLV for short — means you bet a better price than the price the line settles at right before kickoff. If you take a team at -3 on Tuesday and the line closes at -5 on Sunday, you got closing line value. You beat the market to the number.

Hypothetical example: say the Cowboys open at -1.5 in Philadelphia on Tuesday and you bet them, then the line moves to -3 by Sunday. Whether the Cowboys win or lose, your bet was the right side of the market move — you paid less for the same ticket. Over a season, consistently beating the close is the cleanest sign your process is finding real edges, because the closing line is usually the sharpest number of the week.
items.takeaway: You cannot control wins and losses, but you can control the price you pay. Chasing closing line value keeps you on the right side of the market's best guess.

items.headline: Week 7 openers vs now: the biggest moves
paragraphs: Week 7 lookahead lines have been out since last week, and the movers are the story. The Browns at Titans flipped 4.5 points — from Tennessee -3 at the open to the Titans +1.5 now. Buccaneers at Panthers swung the same amount, from Carolina +1.5 to Carolina -3.

Also moving: Colts at Vikings from Minnesota -2.5 to -5.5, Dolphins at Jets from the Jets -2.5 to -4.5, Broncos at Cardinals from Arizona +7.5 to +5.5, Packers at Lions from Detroit -1.5 to -3.0, and Giants at Texans from Houston -5.5 to -7.0. Totals dropped hard in three spots: Browns-Titans 41.5 to 37.5, Colts-Vikings 46.5 to 43.5, Dolphins-Jets 41.5 to 38.5.

No new movement since Sunday — the numbers match the weekend read exactly. Thursday's opener: Patriots at Bears, Chicago -1.5 with a 48.5 total. When the app's Week 7 board lands this morning, compare its market board against these numbers and run anything you like through Check at your book's price.
items.takeaway: The market has spoken on seven games since the open. New information — Hurts, injuries, Thursday reports — is what moves these next.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: Patriots at Bears is two days out (8:15 p.m. ET kickoff Thursday). Chicago's final injury report lands Wednesday, inactives come about 90 minutes before kickoff Thursday, and the board refreshes every morning — so check back in tomorrow's brief for the app's first real Week 7 cards.
One more thing: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log last night's Monday-night result — win or lose — before the Week 7 slate starts.
items.takeaway: Two days to Thursday. Let the board refresh, let the reports land, then Check your price.

evidence.fact: Eagles announced Monday: further testing revealed deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli in Jalen Hurts; clinically stable, expected full recovery, but on blood thinners and barred from contact activities — expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Hurts was placed on IR Saturday and missed Sunday's loss to Carolina; Tanner McKee expected to start. Eagles host Cowboys Sunday.
evidence.interpretation: Season-ending QB change for a Sunday home game; market may still be repricing.
